tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description begins with imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent (assessing/auditing Bedrock security posture), explicitly lists trigger contexts including cases where the user doesn't name a specific control (guardrails, KMS, VPC endpoints, agent IAM, logging), and is a concise paragraph.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when the user wants to assess, audit, or review the security posture of Amazon Bedrock generative-AI workloads in an AWS account, across regions or associated accounts. Apply it even when the user does not name a specific control..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense with domain-specific, non-obvious facts (SDK/IAM prefix mismatch, verify-vs-prescribe contract, global vs regional check handling, AWS-owned key semantics) rather than generic explanations of concepts the agent already knows. There is no filler explaining what Bedrock, IAM, or KMS are in general terms.
tests.evidence: Mind the difference between the SDK client and the IAM action prefix: Bedrock prompts, agents, knowledge bases, flows, and agent action groups are called through the bedrock-agent SDK client ... but their IAM actions use the bedrock: prefix

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed check-by-check reference data (31 checks, API lists, severities) is explicitly placed in references/bedrock-checks.md and referenced, not embedded in the body. The body only contains the verify-vs-prescribe principles and workflow, not lookup tables.
tests.evidence: Open [references/bedrock-checks.md](references/bedrock-checks.md) and execute every check. Each entry gives the read-only API call(s), the pass/fail/N-A logic, severity, verifiability, resolution text, and a documentation reference URL

tests.reasoning: Both files in references/ are linked with markdown link syntax in the body.

tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by context specifying when/why to load it (e.g., during region resolution, during check execution, during report assembly).
tests.evidence: See [references/finding-schema-and-report.md](references/finding-schema-and-report.md) → "Region resolution". In short: ... Open [references/bedrock-checks.md](references/bedrock-checks.md) and execute every check.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths from the skill root with no traversal or absolute paths.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile/safety-critical sections (read-only guardrail, verify-vs-prescribe contract) are highly prescriptive with exact rules, while flexible parts (scope negotiation with the user, report assembly) allow reasonable agent judgment. This matches fragility to prescriptiveness well.
tests.evidence: NEVER call any API that creates, updates, deletes, attaches, enables, disables, or otherwise mutates a resource... Never call a non-Get/List/Describe verb

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: No competing tool/approach menus are presented; the skill prescribes a single consistent methodology (read-only API checks per reference file) without offering multiple equivalent tools.
tests.evidence: Skill does not present alternative tools/approaches as a menu; it consistently directs to the single defined check methodology.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable procedure (confirm scope, resolve regions, run checks, validate, report) applicable to any Bedrock assessment request, not a one-off declarative task.
tests.evidence:
- [ ] Step 1: Confirm intent and scope (read-only, accounts in scope)
- [ ] Step 2: Resolve target regions
- [ ] Step 3: Run every Bedrock check per region (BR-01..BR-31)

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes concrete, non-obvious environment-specific corrections functioning as gotchas (e.g., SDK/IAM prefix mismatch, AWS-owned key reporting rule, Prescribe-only BR-12 exception), satisfying the gotchas need for this domain.
